task: DISTILLED SECONDARY FINE-TUNE INTO K2 - feasibility and exact plan
summary: FEASIBLE, not a sure win. y3uanm's v1 distilled secondary fine-tune (teacher = pilkwang seed314159, sha 9bac2fa0...; only the last decoder block + heads trainable; BN frozen; softplus at GT voxels + 0.5 teacher-BCE + 0.1 feature MSE; lr 1e-5; batch 1; 1 epoch over 199 videos = 19,701 it) runs on a Kaggle T4 with only public inputs (support pack + seed314159 + competition data; zebrahub and deepcenter are attached but unused; v2 needs a non-public synthetic dataset). Estimated ~2.7-6 h per epoch on 1x T4, GPU memory < 6 GB. y3uanm's wall time is unmeasured: their notebooks carry no outputs and the API returned 429. Their output uses the same weights layout as x138, but x138 hard-codes the secondary sha (code cell 3) and wants model.weight_sha256 in the manifest. So we need a new private dataset with our own manifest plus a one-line builder patch `--patch secswap` (env BIOHUB_SECONDARY_EXPECTED_SHA256; BIOHUB_SECONDARY_ARTIFACT_MANIFEST already exists). The finals rebuild stays byte-identical. Honest gate: FT on 44b6 only -> K2 train lab on the 39 held-out 6bba exp60 clips (kill if < -0.0005), plus a detection-count proxy and a dummy. Timeline if the user OKs by ~21:00Z: training 21:45Z -> gate/dummy ~04:30-05:00Z 27 Sep -> submit ~05:00-06:00Z -> public score ~13:00Z 27 Sep. Latest start: training by ~29 Sep 02:30Z (Kaggle tick limit), or 28 Sep 19:00Z under our R8. Honest expectation: E[delta public] ~ +0.0005, P(>= 0.955) ~25-35%, P(>= 0.956) ~10%. y3uanm's 0.949 -> 0.956 came AFTER their FT notebooks existed, so it is not attributable to the FT. Our earlier non-distilled swap lost 0.007. #37 is never dropped; the FT replaces #38 only if public >= 0.955 and the gate passes. Needs the user's explicit R9 lift for this item. Notes: research/wf_ideas_v4/reach0955/r_retrain.notes.md

items.what: FEASIBILITY (a): the y3uanm v1 recipe runs on Kaggle almost as-is. Build our training kernel exp70 from notebook0afc5663f6 (cells 2-6 verbatim) with 5 small changes. Two copies: exp70a = all 199 videos (the production secondary); exp70b = 44b6-only (the gate model, RT-3).
items.evidence: experiments/ext_y3uanm-secondary-ft/notebook0afc5663f6.ipynb + kernel-metadata_0afc5663f6.json. INPUTS: pilkwang/biohub-tracking-support-pack-50ep-v1 (repo + offline wheels, installed with --no-index --no-deps), pilkwang/biohub-temporal-unet3d-seed314159-v1 (teacher = initial weights; the notebook asserts sha256 9bac2fa0..., the same file x138 checks), competition train (199 annotated .zarr+.geff). pilkwang/biohub-deepcenter-unet3d-center-prior-v1 and hftams/zebrahub-zsns003 are attached but UNUSED: zebrahub appears only in a commented-out `ls` cell. I could not verify whether it is public (Kaggle API 429). v2 (notebook0afc5663955) also needs y3uanm/biohub-synthetic-dataset-jose, which is NOT public, so v2 cannot be reproduced; its 10 epochs would not fit in time either. RECIPE: freeze everything except unet.decoder_blocks[-1], unet.head and detect_head; train() is forced to eval (BN and dropout frozen); det loss = softplus(-logit) at the GT voxels + 0.5*BCE to the teacher's sigmoid on every non-GT voxel + 0.1*normalised feature MSE to the teacher; edge loss unchanged through the frozen transformer; AdamW lr 1e-5, batch 1, fp32 (the support-pack trainer has no AMP), num_workers 0, seed 314159, 1 GPU, no validation, 1 epoch. Windows per video = T-W+1 = 99, so one epoch = 19,701 it (6bba-only 12,672, 44b6-only 7,029). The pulled notebooks carry NO outputs, and 3 kernels-output calls hit 429, so y3uanm's wall time is unmeasured and it is not even proven their run finished. Our timing anchors: exp23 = 1,200 it at batch 8 with AMP on 2xT4 in 27.7 min (forward 35%, backward 64%, data 1%); exp01 = 3.4 s/it fp32 batch 8 on 2xT4. ESTIMATE on 1x T4 fp32 batch 1: 0.5-1.1 s/it (teacher forward + student forward + partial backward + zarr read in the main thread), so v1 = ~2.7-6 h per 199-video epoch (central ~4 h); with num_workers=4 ~2.2-4.5 h. 3 epochs = ~7-15 h (not safe inside the 12 h limit); 5 epochs does not fit. GPU memory < ~6 GB (inputs 2x64x64x64 after the (1,4,4) downsample; two 8.4 MB models), so a T4 16 GB is fine. Avoid the P100 (recent Kaggle torch builds may lack sm_60). Friend A's RTX 5070 Ti (all 199 videos local) would run ~2-3x faster; availability unknown.

items.what: SWAP MECHANICS (b): publish the weights as a new private dataset and add the smallest builder change, `--patch secswap`, so a K2 build loads our secondary. The finals rebuild stays byte-identical.
items.evidence: x138 code cell 3 (experiments/ext_x138/biohub-x138.ipynb): the manifest path comes from env BIOHUB_SECONDARY_ARTIFACT_MANIFEST (default /kaggle/input/datasets/pilkwang/biohub-temporal-unet3d-seed314159-v1/ARTIFACT_MANIFEST.json). The finder accepts a manifest only if json['model']['weight_sha256'] == _secondary_expected_sha256, and that sha is HARD-CODED ('9bac2fa0...', not an env knob). Explicit paths are tried first, then an rglob over /kaggle/input (~210 s). The loader then copies <root>/weights or weights.zip, hard-checks the sha of weights/unet_transformer/split_0/edge_predictor_best.pth (+ config.json) and sets BIOHUB_SECONDARY_WEIGHTS. Detection weight 0.80: fused det = 0.2*primary + 0.8*secondary, mean/std-aligned to the primary per frame (scale ratio clamped 0.5-2). Edge weight 0.15, low_margin_consensus, edge-feature TTA 0.75. y3uanm's own ARTIFACT_MANIFEST has a TOP-LEVEL 'sha256', so x138 would NOT find it as-is: our manifest must carry model.weight_sha256. The weights format is identical: a plain state_dict with 'unet.' keys plus the original config.json (window 2, downsample 1,4,4; load_model checks that the grid matches the primary). tools/build_probe_kernel.py has no secondary patch. --set appends os.environ lines to config cell 2, which runs before cell 3, so env knobs work once the sha line reads one. The V1284 coordinate head reads PRIMARY features, so a secondary swap does not break it; the fused centres it refines do move.

items.what: HONEST GATE (c): a cross-embryo check of the recipe. The FT trained on 44b6 only (exp70b) replaces the secondary in the K2 train lab on the 39 held-out 6bba exp60 clips (official metric, K2 tail replayed). An in-kernel detection proxy runs first. This is a kill gate (it detects harm) and cannot prove a gain.
items.evidence: exp60 train lab (experiments/exp60_trainlab/split.json: 6bba 39 clips / 88 GT divisions; 44b6 17 clips / 11). The control and ins35 arms already exist, so only the swapped arm needs GPU. Lab kernel times: shard A 116.5 min (28 clips), B 93.7 min, so 39 6bba clips = ~2.5-3 h on one T4. tools/trainlab.py score (--dumps --nb --only --out --workers) exists. The pilkwang teacher saw all 199 videos (both embryos), so no leak-free detector test exists. Training the FT on 44b6 only makes the FT *delta* out-of-sample on 6bba, which is the most honest test that fits the time. 44b6->6bba over 6bba->44b6: the 6bba bed has more power (39 vs 17 clips), and 44b6-only training is the shortest (7,029 it). Precision cannot be measured on sparse GT (~6% annotated), so a detection-count ratio is the harm proxy (exp23's losing swap had +3.9% nodes).
items.expected_public_gain: None directly. It stops a harmful swap before a slot and the finals are spent. Power is low: effects below ~0.001 will read as ties.
items.steps: PRE-REGISTER before any result. G0 (training sanity, in exp70a/b): finite losses, only the 3 trainable modules changed, new sha != parent. Push it; download to _dl/exp71; then python tools/trainlab.py score --dumps _dl/exp71 --nb experiments/exp71_secft_lab6bba/<nb>.ipynb --only <the 39 stems> --out experiments/exp71_secft_lab6bba/results --workers 4; compare per clip with experiments/exp60_trainlab/results.json on the same stems (arms control and ins35). PASS = parity true, pooled ins35 delta >= -0.0005 and no more losing clips than winning. KILL if delta < -0.0005, a division-J drop > 0.01 or a node delta > +3%. If G1 fails, skip G2 and stop the line.

items.what: SUBMISSION CANDIDATE (d): exp72 = K2 (#37 stack, unchanged) with only the secondary swapped for the all-199 distilled FT. Dummy run, gates, then ONE public probe (needs the user's OK).
items.evidence: K2 dummy 25.6 min (_dl/biohub-exp58-x138-safe-lowref; 121,252 final nodes); K2 hidden run clean at 7.36-7.54 h against the 9.5 h safetail deadline. Team y3uanm: 0.949 (24 Sep 10:37) -> 0.956, but their FT notebooks date from 21-22 Sep (BEFORE the 0.949), so the jump coincides with the x138 era and is NOT attributable to the FT. The v2 they may have used had 10 epochs + non-public synthetic data. Our earlier swap (exp23: sparse BCE, lr 5e-5, all layers, no teacher) lost 0.007 on the LB (0.937 vs 0.944, +3.9% nodes). The distilled recipe is far more conservative (lr 1e-5, 3 modules, teacher BCE on unlabelled voxels), so a small effect either way is likely. Our lab->public transfer has been ~1/6.
items.expected_public_gain: Honest prior: E[delta public] ~ +0.0005 (range -0.002..+0.003); P(public >= 0.955) ~25-35%, P(>= 0.956) ~10%, P(< 0.954) ~25%. Reaching 0.957 from this item alone is unlikely.
items.private_risk: Moderate-low. (1) The secondary carries 0.8 of the fused detection map, so any change hits every detection. (2) The V1284 head, lowrefine, the DaughterNet insertion thresholds and x138's thresholds were fitted to the ORIGINAL fusion (distribution shift). (3) Sparse-label suppression is mitigated by the teacher BCE, not removed (softplus only at annotated voxels). (4) Embryo overfit: the FT sees both train embryos while the private set is other embryos. (5) Public = one embryo (~29% of test), so a +0.001 public gain is within selection noise. (6) Runtime: more detections slow the ILP; safetail keeps the 9.5 h cap. #37 is never dropped.
